hunt.justification: M365 identities are the gateway to corporate data. Session hijacking and over-permissioned apps allow attackers to bypass standard MFA and maintain persistence even after password resets. This hunt ensures that the highest levels of tenant access are only held by legitimate, authorized personnel.

related.reason: ClickFix focuses on the endpoint PowerShell execution portion of the attack, whereas this hunt focuses on the resulting cloud identity abuse.

meta.analysis: A standing detection rule for Global Admin assignment often creates alert fatigue in active tenants. This hunt pivots between logon protocols (device code flow), MFA changes, and role management to provide the full context of a takeover chain that a single rule would miss.

stages.name: Social Engineering Phishing
observables: Email subjects regarding holiday policy updates
Look-alike SharePoint domains
Short codes (Netflix-style) for device login

stages.name: ClickFix PowerShell Execution
observables: powershell.exe
Windows key + R (Run dialog) instructions
Clipboard manipulation via fake CAPTCHA 'prove you are not a robot'
PowerShell commands designed to export session cookies

stages.name: Session Hijacking via Token Theft
observables: Cookie Editor browser extension
Access to Outlook from unexpected IP addresses with existing session cookies
Successful sign-ins bypassing MFA using stolen tokens

stages.name: Attacker MFA Registration
observables: Registration of new MFA methods (phone numbers or authenticators) by a recently compromised account
Entra ID audit events for MFA device changes

stages.name: App Registration Secret Manipulation
observables: New secrets created for existing App Registrations
Secrets with long lifespans (e.g., 2 years)
Standard user accounts interacting with the Azure management portal/Entra app registrations

stages.name: Privilege Escalation via Over-Permissioned Apps
observables: Apps with 'RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory' permissions
n8n workflow automation tool usage
Assignment of Global Administrator role to a compromised user via an application principal

stages.name: Device Code Flow Hijacking
observables: Logins via microsoft.com/devicelogin
Device code flow used for browser-based session capture
Unusual UserAgents or client applications requesting device codes

scenario.summary: Attackers target Microsoft 365 environments using social engineering tactics like ClickFix and Device Code phishing to bypass MFA or capture session tokens. Once inside, they exploit over-permissioned applications and register new MFA methods to persist and escalate privileges to Global Administrator.

meta.rationale: Focus first on users with Global Administrator or Application Administrator roles. If initial access signals are found, widen the scope to all active Entra ID users to check for broader lateral movement.
meta.hypothesis: An attacker has hijacked an M365 session via device-code flow or token theft, modified MFA for persistence, and abused over-permissioned applications to escalate to Global Administrator.

blind_spots.risk: Persistent MFA methods added by an attacker can remain invisible if audit logging is not enabled for the specific tenant or user.
blind_spots.question: if MFA modifications occurred more than 90 days ago or if logging is disabled
blind_spots.requires: hb_cloud_api_activity with M365 Unified Audit Log (UAL) data

blind_spots.risk: The hunt can see the cloud-side result of session hijacking but cannot see the tool (Cookie Editor) or process (browser) if it occurs on a device without telemetry.
blind_spots.question: if the initial session theft occurred on a personal or unmanaged device
blind_spots.requires: Endpoint agent on all devices accessing M365

hunt.name: M365 Identity Takeover and Application Abuse
hunt.description: This hunt targets the cloud-plane aftermath of identity compromise. It identifies the EvilTokens device-code flow pattern and subsequent persistence actions in Entra ID. The hunt uses a phased approach: it first isolates suspicious logins and MFA modifications, then examines high-impact behaviors like application secret creation and privileged role assignments. This progression helps analysts distinguish routine administrative changes from a coordinated account takeover attempt.

config.scoping_notes: Focus first on users with Global Administrator or Application Administrator roles. If initial access signals are found, widen the scope to all active Entra ID users to check for broader lateral movement.
config.beyond_detection: A standing detection rule for Global Admin assignment often creates alert fatigue in active tenants. This hunt pivots between logon protocols (device code flow), MFA changes, and role management to provide the full context of a takeover chain that a single rule would miss.

config.content: SELECT username, email, privileged, mfa_enabled, last_sign_in FROM hb_users WHERE provider = 'azure_ad' AND status = 'active' AND privileged = 'true'
config.description: Identify active privileged accounts to focus the investigation on the most high-impact potential takeover targets.
config.expected_signal: A list of privileged accounts. A lack of MFA on these accounts is an immediate security gap.

primitive_config.label: Scope privileged Azure AD identities
primitive_config.content: SELECT username, email, privileged, mfa_enabled, last_sign_in FROM hb_users WHERE provider = 'azure_ad' AND status = 'active' AND privileged = 'true'
primitive_config.expected: A list of privileged accounts. A lack of MFA on these accounts is an immediate security gap.

config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, src_endpoint_hostname, actor_user_name, client_app, time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE provider = 'm365' AND (('{{device_code_app_id}}' <> '' AND app_id = '{{device_code_app_id}}') OR client_app LIKE '%DeviceCode%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_hostname || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_users}}' || ',', ',' || actor_user_name || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify logons via the device code flow, which is used by Phishing-as-a-Service platforms like EvilTokens to capture sessions.
config.expected_signal: Logons from unexpected IPs using the device code flow. Zero results proves absence for the given window and parameters.

primitive_config.label: Device code flow sign-in activity
primitive_config.content: SELECT src_endpoint_ip, src_endpoint_hostname, actor_user_name, client_app, time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE provider = 'm365' AND (('{{device_code_app_id}}' <> '' AND app_id = '{{device_code_app_id}}') OR client_app LIKE '%DeviceCode%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_hostname || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || src_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_users}}' || ',', ',' || actor_user_name || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Logons from unexpected IPs using the device code flow. Zero results proves absence for the given window and parameters.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, target_user_name, api_operation, target_modified_property_names, time FROM hb_cloud_api_activity WHERE provider = 'm365' AND api_operation IN ('Update user', 'Set-MsolUser') AND instr(LOWER(target_modified_property_names), 'strongauthenticationmethod') > 0 AND ('{{scope_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_users}}' || ',', ',' || actor_user_name || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect changes to authentication methods that attackers use to secure persistent access to a compromised account.
config.expected_signal: A record of a user modifying their own or another user's MFA methods. This is suspicious if it occurs near a device-code logon.

config.objective: Analyze the timing between device-code logons and MFA modifications to identify likely session hijackings.
config.description: Evaluate the sign-in and MFA evidence together to determine if an account takeover has occurred.
config.expected_signal: A list of accounts with high takeover probability based on the combined evidence.
config.success_criteria: A per-account verdict citing the specific logon and modification rows.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, api_operation, COUNT(DISTINCT target_user_name) AS targets, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_cloud_api_activity WHERE provider = 'm365' AND (api_operation = 'Add password' OR (api_operation = 'Add member to role' AND (instr(LOWER(target_modified_property_new_values), 'company administrator') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(target_modified_property_new_values), 'global administrator') > 0))) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY actor_user_name, api_operation ORDER BY targets ASC
config.description: Identify rare users performing administrative role assignments or creating application secrets, which signals the transition from beachhead to full tenant control.
config.expected_signal: Rare users creating app secrets or assigning Global Admin roles. If only one user is doing this who isn't a known admin, it is highly malicious.
